links.outcome: Calibration/probability accuracy on external NHANES hold-out before vs after local recalibration
links.effect: Brier score fell from 0.286 to 0.109 and log loss from 1.253 to 0.388 after recalibration; AUC 0.826 vs 0.810; calibration intercept 0.103, slope 0.684.
links.quote: Probability accuracy improved significantly: the Brier score decreased from 0.286 to 0.109, and the log loss from 1.253 to 0.388.

links.outcome: Performance on external population versus internal test set
links.effect: Internal test AUC 0.995 versus external NHANES hold-out AUC 0.826 before recalibration and 0.810 after; miscalibration before recalibration.
links.quote: On the hold-out validation subset, discrimination was good before recalibration (AUC = 0.826) (Fig. 5 A) and remained similar after applying the fixed calibrator (AUC = 0.810).

links.effect: External raw calibration was poor: Brier 0.286 and log loss 1.253 before recalibration; domain shift was reduced but not eliminated.
links.quote: Outcomes were defined by ultrasound in development and by CAP in external validation, so threshold and sensitivity differences can cause domain shift; recalibration reduced but did not eliminate this issue, and confirmation with additional imaging standards is needed.

links.effect: XGBoost best: AUC 0.995, F1 0.955, accuracy 0.992, precision/specificity 1.000, sensitivity 0.914; RF second AUC 0.990.
links.quote: XGBoost demonstrated the best discrimination (AUC 0.995) and, at the F1-max threshold, the strongest overall classification performance with an F1 score (F1) of 0.955, accuracy (ACC) of 0.992, precision (PRE) of 1.000, specificity (SPE) of 1.000, and sensitivity (SEN) of 0.914.
